correctedState: Not a divergence. The doc sentence is confirmed verbatim (sessions.md:272) and the fork does exactly what it describes: it sets CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, so SDK transcripts live under it. The cited code facts are all true -- options.ts:255 sets it to <workspaceRoot>/claude-config from NESSY_WORKSPACE_ID, there is no migration of pre-existing ~/.claude/projects transcripts, and no config-dir fallback lookup -- but none of the three is a defect. (a) No fallback lookup is possible to omit: workspaceClaudeConfigDir (options.ts:221-226) is a pure deterministic function of the Workspace id, so within a Workspace the write path and the read path are the same path on every spawn; steady-state resume is unaffected. (b) The axis the Tip actually warns about, <encoded-cwd>, is handled deliberately and with more machinery than the page describes: sdkCwd is pinned at session creation and never moved (claude-agent.ts:1260-1266; SessionManager.ts:14319-14325 preserveSdkCwd), a fork spawns at the parent's sdkCwd (SessionManager.ts:9088-9091), and resolveSpawnCwd (claude-agent.ts:3045-3067) is a four-candidate existence-checked chain. (c) The SDK jsonl is not the resume corpus of record: sessions/mirror/types.ts:5 states local disk 'is written FIRST and stays authoritative', StoredSession.messages is the user-visible transcript, and SessionManager.ts:18950-18953 regenerates sdkCwd on a cross-server move precisely because the SDK file does not travel. (d) A missed SDK transcript is detected, not silent: claude-agent.ts:1937-1966 catches the SDK's empty resume, clears sdkSessionId, and replays Nessy's own messages via buildRecoveryContext (base-agent.ts:1944-1971 / SessionManager.ts:11913) with a visible 'Restoring conversation context...' status. So the whole exposure of 'no migration' is one bounded context truncation on the first post-upgrade turn of a pre-existing session. The per-Workspace redirect is a recorded decision: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-isolation-hardening.md:82-95 Task 3, whose gate is 'two workspaces do not see each other's config', and its session-history consequence was already written down at docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:166. The only accurate residual is cosmetic: the options.ts:184-196 doc-comment says 'TWO HAZARDS :356 NAMES' while env-vars.md:356 enumerates four items; a one-line amendment noting that per-Workspace session history is the intent, that plugins were already redirected by plugins/data-paths.ts:115/131, and that pre-Task-3 sessions land in buildRecoveryContext on first resume would make the comment match the sentence it quotes. Separately, that plan carries no ## Tracker section, which the repo's Editing Rules require.
